title: Understanding Nouns and Verbs in Simple Sentences

blocks.text: Have you ever wondered what makes a sentence complete? In English, two important parts of speech are nouns and verbs. Nouns name people, places, things, or ideas, while verbs express actions or states of being.

blocks.markdown: In this lesson, we will explore nouns and verbs in simple sentences. A **noun** is a word that names a person, place, thing, or idea. For example, in the sentence 'The dog barks,' 'dog' is a noun. A **verb** is a word that shows action or a state of being. In the same sentence, 'barks' is the verb because it describes what the dog is doing.

blocks.title: Definition of Nouns
blocks.text: Nouns are words that name people, places, things, or ideas. They can be singular (one) or plural (more than one).

blocks.markdown: Nouns can be classified into different types: proper nouns (specific names like 'Lagos' or 'Mary'), common nouns (general names like 'city' or 'girl'), and collective nouns (names for groups like 'team' or 'flock'). Verbs also have different forms, including the simple present (e.g., 'run', 'eat') and the simple past (e.g., 'ran', 'ate').

blocks.title: Identifying Nouns and Verbs
blocks.prompt: Identify the nouns and verbs in the following sentence: 'The teacher teaches the students.'

steps.text: First, find the nouns in the sentence. Here, 'teacher' and 'students' are nouns.
Next, identify the verb. The word 'teaches' is the verb because it shows the action performed by the teacher.

blocks.markdown: When forming sentences, it is important to ensure that the verb agrees with the subject. For example, 'The cat runs' (singular) and 'The cats run' (plural). Notice how the verb changes depending on whether the subject is singular or plural.

blocks.title: Tip for Exam Success
blocks.text: Always check if the verb agrees with the subject in number. This is a common area where students make mistakes.

points: Nouns name people, places, things, or ideas.
Verbs show actions or states of being.
Ensure verbs agree with their subjects in number.
